mainTopic: Combining עירוב חצרות and שיתוף מבואות, and how many עירוב contributions groups in one divided hall must make
overview: This amud opens with the second opinion in a dispute about where רבי מאיר and חכמים disagree over needing both an עירוב חצרות and a שיתוף מבואות. That opinion says that with wine everyone requires both, and the argument is only about bread. The גמרא challenges this from the ברייתא's wording. רב גידל in the name of רב answers that both options in the ברייתא use bread. Three אמוראים then rule in favor of רבי מאיר, but at different strengths: הלכה, מנהג, or נהגו העם. A new משנה follows about five groups spending שבת in one divided hall. בית שמאי require a separate עירוב for each group, while בית הלל say one is enough, unless the groups are in separate rooms or upper stories. The גמרא then asks what kind of divider the משנה means. It brings two versions of רב נחמן's view about a peg partition, and two opposite views from רבי חייא and רבי שמעון ברבי about partitions that do or do not reach the ceiling.

steps.title: The second view: the dispute is only about bread
steps.stepSummary: The second אמורא says that with wine everyone requires both an עירוב and a שיתוף. רבי מאיר and חכמים argue only when bread was used.
steps.simpleTranslation: And one said: With wine, everyone agrees that we need two (both an עירוב and a שיתוף). Where they argue is with bread.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a two-sided disagreement between אמוראים. Here the second אמורא explains which case רבי מאיר and חכמים are really arguing about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Wine is not a valid food for an עירוב חצרות, so a שיתוף made with wine cannot also cover the courtyards. That is why everyone agrees both are needed. With bread, which is valid for courtyards too, חכמים say one is enough, but רבי מאיר still demands both.

keyTerms.meaning: And one (of the two אמוראים) said
Everyone agrees; there is no dispute
Two, meaning both an עירוב and a שיתוף
Bread
Wine

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two kinds of joining. An עירוב חצרות joins houses into one courtyard. A שיתוף מבואות joins courtyards into one alleyway. The question here is whether one of them can do the job of both.

phrases.english: And one said:
phrases.notes: The second side of the dispute. The first side came on the previous amud.

phrases.english: with wine, everyone agrees
phrases.notes: Meaning a שיתוף made with wine.

phrases.english: that we require two,
phrases.notes: Both an עירוב and a שיתוף.

phrases.english: where they disagree is with bread.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the two-sided dispute that began on the previous amud by giving the second opinion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Wine: everyone requires both. Bread: רבי מאיר requires both, while חכמים say one suffices.

steps.title: Challenge from the ברייתא's wording
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא quotes חכמים saying 'either an עירוב or a שיתוף.' The גמרא suggests this means a שיתוף with wine is enough, which contradicts the second view.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged: 'And חכמים say: either one makes an עירוב or one makes a שיתוף.' Doesn't this mean either an עירוב in the courtyard with bread, or a שיתוף in the alleyway with wine?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the second view using the ברייתא itself. It proposes that חכמים allow a wine שיתוף alone, which would mean they argue even about wine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The usual practice is an עירוב with bread and a שיתוף with wine. So 'either one' seems to say even a wine שיתוף alone works for חכמים. That directly contradicts the claim that with wine everyone agrees both are needed.

keyTerms.meaning: They make an עירוב, joining houses in a courtyard
They make a שיתוף, merging courtyards in an alleyway
Does it not mean...? (a suggested reading used to attack)
Alleyway
Courtyard

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
And the Rabbis say
either one makes an eruv or one makes a merging.
Does it not mean:
either one makes an eruv in the courtyard with bread,
or one makes a merging in the alleyway with wine?
phrases.notes: If the text really says this, then חכמים would allow a שיתוף with wine all by itself.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the second opinion from step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that with wine everyone requires both.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא seems to let חכמים use a wine שיתוף alone, so they must argue about wine too.

steps.title: Rereading: both options use bread
steps.stepSummary: רב גידל in the name of רב explains that both of חכמים's options use bread. Either an עירוב or a שיתוף made with bread permits carrying in both the courtyard and the alleyway.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב גידל said in the name of רב: This is what it means. Either one makes an עירוב in the courtyard with bread, and it is permitted here and there. Or one makes a שיתוף in the alleyway with bread, and it is permitted here and there.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the second view by explaining the ברייתא differently. 'Either-or' refers to two uses of bread, not to wine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since bread is valid for both an עירוב and a שיתוף, either one made with bread can cover both areas. The ברייתא never says a wine שיתוף alone works, so the claim that with wine everyone needs both still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it means (a rereading of a source)
They are permitted to carry
Here and there, meaning both the courtyard and the alleyway

steps.whatToRemember: According to this view, bread can do double duty, so one joining is enough for חכמים. Wine cannot do double duty, so everyone requires both.

phrases.english: Rav Giddel said that Rav said,
this is what it is saying:
either one makes an eruv in the courtyard with bread,
and they are permitted here and there,
phrases.notes: Both in the courtyard and in the alleyway.

phrases.english: or one makes a merging in the alleyway with bread,
phrases.notes: Notice it says bread here, not wine. That's the key change in this version.

phrases.english: and they are permitted here and there.

steps.terutzHavaAmina: The שיתוף in the ברייתא was made with wine.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both options in the ברייתא use bread, which works for both areas, so wine is not discussed.

steps.title: Three levels of ruling for רבי מאיר
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה in the name of רב says the הלכה follows רבי מאיר. רב הונא says it is only a מנהג. רבי יוחנן says the people simply took on this practice.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: The הלכה follows רבי מאיר. רב הונא said: The custom follows רבי מאיר. רבי יוחנן said: The people are accustomed to follow רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now gives the practical ruling. Three אמוראים agree in favor of רבי מאיר but disagree about how strong that ruling is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'הלכה' means we teach it publicly as the rule. 'מנהג' means we do not announce it, but we instruct someone who asks to follow it. 'נהגו העם' is the weakest: we do not instruct it, but if people already do it we do not stop them.

keyTerms.meaning: Binding law, taught publicly
Custom; told to someone who asks but not announced
The people took on this practice; not taught, but not stopped

steps.whatToRemember: All three side with רבי מאיר, who requires both an עירוב and a שיתוף. They differ only on the level of authority: הלכה, then מנהג, then נהגו העם.
steps.whyThisMatters: These three terms are a standard ladder of ruling strength found throughout ש״ס.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
The halakha is in accordance with Rabbi Meir.
And Rav Huna said:
The custom is in accordance with Rabbi Meir.
phrases.notes: One who asks is instructed to do this.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan said:
The people are accustomed to follow Rabbi Meir.
phrases.notes: Nobody is told to do this, but if people do it, we don't object.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from analyzing the dispute to deciding the practical ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The practice follows רבי מאיר, requiring both an עירוב and a שיתוף. Its strength is debated: הלכה, מנהג, or נהגו העם.

steps.title: Five groups in one hall: one עירוב or five?
steps.stepSummary: The משנה presents a case of five groups in one divided hall. בית שמאי require an עירוב for each group, and בית הלל say one עירוב is enough for all.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Five groups spent שבת in one big hall. בית שמאי say each group needs its own עירוב. בית הלל say one עירוב is enough for all of them.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה opens with a case: one big hall is split into sections, and five groups stay in it over שבת. בית שמאי and בית הלל argue about how many עירוב contributions are needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The real question is whether each section of the hall counts as its own 'house'. בית שמאי treat each group as a separate household, so each must join the courtyard's עירוב separately. בית הלל treat the whole hall as one household, so one contribution covers everyone.

keyTerms.meaning: Short for מַתְנִיתִין, 'our משנה'
Groups of people (eating and staying together)
A large hall or reception room
A shared food deposit that lets residents carry in a shared courtyard on שבת

steps.confusionAlert: The argument is not about whether an עירוב is needed at all. Everyone agrees one is needed for the shared courtyard. The argument is only about how many separate contributions the hall's groups must make.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
Five groups
who spent Shabbat in one hall
phrases.notes: The hall is divided into sections, and each section opens into a shared courtyard.

phrases.english: Beit Shammai say:
an eiruv for each and every group
And Beit Hillel say:
one eiruv for all of them

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה on a new topic, separate from the earlier discussion of רבי מאיר and חכמים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בית שמאי: a separate עירוב for each group. בית הלל: one עירוב for all.

steps.title: Groups in separate rooms or upper floors need separate עירוב
steps.stepSummary: בית הלל agree that when some of the groups live in separate rooms or upper stories, each group needs its own עירוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: בית הלל agree that if some of the groups are staying in separate rooms or upper floors, each group needs its own עירוב.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה limits בית הלל's ruling. When groups are in truly separate rooms or upstairs, even בית הלל require a separate עירוב for each.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This shows that בית הלל's 'one עירוב' applies only to a single hall with internal dividers. A real separate room or upper floor is a separate dwelling, so being in the same building does not make the groups one household.

keyTerms.meaning: And they agree (one side concedes a point)
Separate rooms
Upper stories, attics

phrases.english: And they concede that when
some of them are staying in rooms
or in upper stories
they need an eiruv
for each and every group

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets a limit on בית הלל's lenient ruling from step 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even בית הלל require a separate עירוב for groups in separate rooms or upper stories.
steps.whatToRemember: בית הלל's 'one עירוב' applies only to sections of one hall. Separate rooms or upper floors always need separate עירוב.

steps.title: רב נחמן: the argument is only about a weak divider
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן says the משנה's argument is about a hall divided by a weak peg partition (מסיפס). With a solid ten-טפח partition, everyone agrees each group needs its own עירוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: רב נחמן said: The argument is when the hall is divided by a peg partition. But if it is divided by a solid partition ten טפחים high, everyone agrees each group needs its own עירוב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins by asking what kind of divider the משנה is talking about. רב נחמן says the argument is only about a flimsy peg divider.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under this view, בית הלל are lenient only because a peg divider is too weak to make separate homes. A real ten-טפח wall clearly creates separate living spaces, so בית הלל agree with בית שמאי there.

keyTerms.meaning: Short for גְּמָרָא, the discussion of the משנה
A light divider made of pegs or slats, not a solid wall
A partition ten טְפָחִים high, a halachically real wall
Everyone agrees

phrases.english: GEMARA:
Rav Nachman said:
The dispute is with a partition of pegs
but with a partition ten handbreadths high
all agree
an eiruv is needed for each and every group

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains which kind of divided hall the משנה's argument is about.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The argument is only over a peg partition. With a ten-טפח partition, all agree each group needs its own עירוב.

steps.title: Second version of רב נחמן: the argument applies even to a peg divider
steps.stepSummary: A second version reports רב נחמן saying the argument exists even with a peg partition, so it is not limited to the weak-divider case.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say רב נחמן said: Even with a peg partition there is an argument.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives another tradition of what רב נחמן said. In this version, the argument is not limited to solid walls but reaches even a flimsy peg partition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first version, a ten-טפח wall settles the matter for everyone. Here, the argument applies even with a real wall, and the word 'even' (אף) means it extends down to a peg partition too. So בית שמאי treat even a peg divider as separating homes, and בית הלל hold one עירוב is enough even with a solid wall.

keyTerms.meaning: Even

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new rabbi arguing with רב נחמן. It is a different report of what רב נחמן himself said.

phrases.english: Some say:
Rav Nachman said:
Even with a partition of pegs there is a dispute

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי, אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן: אַף בִּמְסִיפָס מַחְלוֹקֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a competing tradition of רב נחמן's statement from step 7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The argument applies even to a peg partition, and all the more so to a ten-טפח wall.

steps.title: First view: the argument is about dividers that reach the ceiling
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא and רבי שמעון ברבי argue about the משנה's case. One says the argument is about partitions reaching the ceiling, and with lower partitions all agree one עירוב is enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא and רבי שמעון ברבי disagreed about this. One said: The argument is about partitions that reach the ceiling. But with partitions that don't reach the ceiling, everyone agrees one עירוב covers them all.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new disagreement between רבי חייא and רבי שמעון ברבי about what the divider in the משנה looks like. This step gives the first opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to this view, only a full floor-to-ceiling divider is strong enough for בית שמאי to call the sections separate homes. A partition that stops short of the ceiling leaves the hall as one space, so even בית שמאי agree one עירוב is enough.

keyTerms.meaning: They disagree about it
One said
Reaching the ceiling

phrases.aramaic: פְּלִיגִי בַּהּ רַבִּי חִיָּיא וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בְּרַבִּי
phrases.english: Rabbi Chiyya and Rabbi Shimon son of Rabbi disagreed about this
One said:
The dispute is about partitions that reach the ceiling
but with partitions that do not reach the ceiling
all agree: one eiruv for all of them

steps.triggerLanguage: פְּלִיגִי בַּהּ רַבִּי חִיָּיא וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בְּרַבִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a new pair of sages, רבי חייא and רבי שמעון ברבי, who also define the משנה's case, this time by whether the partitions reach the ceiling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The argument is about ceiling-high partitions. With lower partitions, everyone agrees one עירוב is enough.

steps.title: Second view: the argument is about dividers that do not reach the ceiling
steps.stepSummary: The other of the two (רבי חייא or רבי שמעון ברבי) says the argument is about partitions that do not reach the ceiling. With ceiling-high partitions, everyone agrees each group needs its own עירוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other said: The argument is about partitions that do not reach the ceiling. But with partitions that reach the ceiling, everyone agrees each group needs its own עירוב.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the second opinion in the disagreement between רבי חייא and רבי שמעון ברבי. It flips the first view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here a ceiling-high partition clearly makes separate homes, so even בית הלל require separate עירוב. The argument is only about lower partitions, which בית שמאי still count as dividing and בית הלל do not. The two views agree that a stronger divider favors separate עירוב. They disagree only about where the line falls.

keyTerms.meaning: And the other one said
They need, they require

steps.whatToRemember: There are two views on the משנה's case. In the first, the argument is over ceiling-high dividers and lower ones need only one עירוב. In the second, the argument is over lower dividers and ceiling-high ones need separate עירוב.
steps.confusionAlert: Watch who says 'one עירוב' and who says 'separate עירוב' in each 'all agree' clause. The two views point in opposite directions.

phrases.english: And one said:
The dispute is about partitions that do not reach the ceiling
but with partitions that reach the ceiling
all agree they need
an eiruv for each and every group

steps.triggerLanguage: וְחַד אָמַר: מַחְלוֹקֶת בִּמְחִיצוֹת שֶׁאֵין מַגִּיעוֹת לַתִּקְרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing opinion to step 9 in the same disagreement.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The argument is about partitions below the ceiling. With ceiling-high partitions, everyone agrees each group needs its own עירוב.
